<p>The Figma MCP server provides the following tools:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="#add_code_connect_map"><code>add_code_connect_map</code></a>: Adds a mapping between a Figma node ID and its corresponding code component in your codebase</li>
<li><a href="#create_new_file"><code>create_new_file</code></a> (remote only): Creates a new blank Figma Design, FigJam, or Figma Slides file in the authenticated user's drafts</li>
<li><a href="#download_assets"><code>download_assets</code></a> (remote only): Downloads rendered exports and original source images from a Figma file</li>
<li><a href="#generate_diagram"><code>generate_diagram</code></a> (remote only): Generates a FigJam diagram from Mermaid syntax</li>
<li><a href="#generate_figma_design"><code>generate_figma_design</code></a> (specific clients only, remote only): Generates design layers from interfaces</li>
<li><a href="#get_code_connect_map"><code>get_code_connect_map</code></a>: Retrieves a mapping between Figma node IDs and their corresponding code components in your codebase</li>
<li><a href="#get_code_connect_suggestions"><code>get_code_connect_suggestions</code></a>: A Figma-prompted tool call to find suggestions for mapping Figma node IDs to their corresponding code components in your codebase using Code Connect</li>
<li><a href="#get_context_for_code_connect"><code>get_context_for_code_connect</code></a> (remote only): A Figma-prompted tool call to get context for generating Code Connect templates</li>
<li><a href="#get_design_context"><code>get_design_context</code></a>: Get the design context for a layer or selection</li>
<li><a href="#get_figjam"><code>get_figjam</code></a>: Converts FigJam diagrams (such as app architecture workflows) to XML</li>
<li><a href="#get_libraries"><code>get_libraries</code></a> (remote only): Returns the libraries currently added to the file (subscribed) and libraries available to add (community UI kits and org libraries)</li>
<li><a href="#get_metadata"><code>get_metadata</code></a>: Returns a sparse XML representation of your selection that contains basic properties such as layer IDs, names, types, position and sizes</li>
<li><a href="#get_motion_context"><code>get_motion_context</code></a>: Returns keyframe animation data (tracks, easing curves, and ready-to-use CSS and motion.dev code snippets) for an animated selection</li>
<li><a href="#get_screenshot"><code>get_screenshot</code></a>: Allows the agent to take a screenshot of your selection</li>
<li><a href="#get_shader_effect"><code>get_shader_effect</code></a>: Retrieves a shader effect and its source files</li>
<li><a href="#get_shader_fill"><code>get_shader_fill</code></a>: Retrieves a shader fill and its source files</li>
<li><a href="#get_variable_defs"><code>get_variable_defs</code></a>: Returns the variables and styles used in your Figma selection</li>
<li><a href="#list_shader_effects"><code>list_shader_effects</code></a>: Lists shader effects in your authenticated account library</li>
<li><a href="#list_shader_fills"><code>list_shader_fills</code></a>: Lists shader fills in your authenticated account library</li>
<li><a href="#search_design_system"><code>search_design_system</code></a> (remote only): Searches design libraries for components, variables, and styles matching a text query</li>
<li><a href="#send_code_connect_mappings"><code>send_code_connect_mappings</code></a>: A Figma-prompted tool used after calling <code>get_code_connect_suggestions</code> to confirm the suggested Code Connect mappings</li>
<li><a href="#upload_assets"><code>upload_assets</code></a> (remote only): Uploads supported assets (PNG, JPG, GIF, and WebP) to a Figma file</li>
<li><a href="#use_figma"><code>use_figma</code></a> (remote only): The general-purpose tool for creating, editing, or inspecting any object in a Figma file</li>
<li><a href="#whoami-remote-only"><code>whoami</code></a> (remote only): Returns the identity of the user that's authenticated to Figma</li>
</ul>
<p>The Figma MCP server also provides the following MCP prompt:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="#create_design_system_rules"><code>create_design_system_rules</code></a>: Creates a rule file that provide agents with the right context to translate designs into frontend code</li>
</ul>

<h2 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="tools">Tools<a href="#tools" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Tools" title="Direct link to Tools" translate="no">​</a></h2>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="add_code_connect_map">add_code_connect_map<a href="#add_code_connect_map" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to add_code_connect_map" title="Direct link to add_code_connect_map" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> Figma Design</p>
<p>Adds a mapping between a Figma node ID and its corresponding code component in your codebase. Setting up these mappings will improve the output quality of design-to-code worksflows and help you identify and use the exact component in your project.</p>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="create_new_file">create_new_file (remote only)<a href="#create_new_file" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to create_new_file (remote only)" title="Direct link to create_new_file (remote only)" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> No file context required</p>
<p>Creates a new blank Figma Design, FigJam, or Figma Slides file in your drafts folder. If you belong to multiple plans, you'll be asked which team or organization to create the file in.</p>
<p><strong>You can ask it to:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Create a new design file</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>create a new Figma file called "Homepage Redesign"</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Create a new FigJam file</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>create a new FigJam board for our project planning session</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Create a new Figma Slides file</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>create a new Figma Slides deck for our Q3 review</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="download_assets">download_assets (remote only)<a href="#download_assets" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to download_assets (remote only)" title="Direct link to download_assets (remote only)" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> Figma Design, FigJam, Figma Slides</p>
<p>Downloads assets from a Figma file. Returns temporary URLs that must be fetched to retrieve file contents.</p>
<p>Each call returns two types of output for the given node(s) — you get both, not one or the other:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Export render:</strong> The node rendered as an image. If the node has export settings configured in Figma, those are used; otherwise it falls back to the defaultFormat and defaultScale parameters (0.01–4x). Without export settings at scale 1, renders are capped at ~4096px on the longest edge. Supports PNG, JPG, SVG, and PDF.</li>
<li><strong>Raw source images:</strong> The original uploaded files (JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP) placed as fills anywhere in the node's subtree, returned without re-rendering. Capped at 20 per call (rawImagesTruncated: true when there are more. Try passing a more specific child node). Useful for cross-file transfer with <code>upload_assets</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Up to 20 nodes can be passed per call.</p>
<h4 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="when-to-use-download_assets-vs-get_screenshot">When to use download_assets vs get_screenshot<a href="#when-to-use-download_assets-vs-get_screenshot" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to When to use download_assets vs get_screenshot" title="Direct link to When to use download_assets vs get_screenshot" translate="no">​</a></h4>
<p>Use get_screenshot when the agent needs to <em>see</em> what a design looks like. Use download_assets when the agent needs to <em>deliver</em> an asset to the user, export in a specific format, or transfer images between files.</p>
<table><thead><tr><th></th><th><strong>get_screenshot</strong></th><th><strong>download_assets</strong></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Use when</strong></td><td>You need to visually inspect a design</td><td>You need to save, deliver, or transfer an asset</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Output</strong></td><td>PNG, inline base64 or URL</td><td>URLs only (PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF, or original source)</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Nodes</strong></td><td>Single</td><td>Up to 20</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Format control</strong></td><td>Always PNG</td><td>PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF (export); original format (raw)</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Original source files</strong></td><td>No — always re-renders</td><td>Yes — raw mode returns the exact uploaded binary</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Inline base64</strong></td><td>Yes, via enableBase64Response</td><td>No</td></tr></tbody></table>
<h4 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="suggested-prompts">Suggested prompts<a href="#suggested-prompts" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to Suggested prompts" title="Direct link to Suggested prompts" translate="no">​</a></h4>
<ul>
<li><strong>Export assets in a specific format</strong>
<ul>
<li>export these icons from my Figma file as SVGs</li>
<li>download the hero image from this frame as a JPG</li>
<li>export this component as a PDF</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Extract original source images</strong>
<ul>
<li>grab the original photos from this mockup</li>
<li>extract the source images from this frame so I can transfer them to another file</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Cross-file image transfer</strong>
<ul>
<li>copy the images from this file into my other Figma file <em>(agent uses download_assets raw mode, then upload_assets)</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="generate_diagram">generate_diagram (remote only)<a href="#generate_diagram" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to generate_diagram (remote only)" title="Direct link to generate_diagram (remote only)" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> No file context required</p>
<p>Generates a FigJam diagram from Mermaid syntax or natural language descriptions. The <code>generate_diagram</code> tool converts structured or inferred diagram definitions into interactive FigJam diagrams that can be edited and shared.</p>
<p>You do not have to provide Mermaid syntax yourself. You can describe the diagram you want in natural language, and the agent will generate the appropriate Mermaid syntax and call the <code>generate_diagram</code> tool automatically.</p>
<p>Diagrams can be created in a new FigJam file or added to an existing FigJam file.</p>
<p>To ensure that the agent uses the Figma MCP <code>generate_diagram</code> tool, you can include the directive "Use the Figma MCP generate_diagram tool" in your prompt. In most cases, the agent will invoke the tool automatically when a diagram is needed.</p>
<p><strong>Supported diagram types:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Flowchart</li>
<li>Gantt chart</li>
<li>State diagram</li>
<li>Sequence diagram</li>
<li>Architecture diagram</li>
<li>Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD)</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Suggested prompts:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Generate a diagram from a description</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>create a flowchart for the user authentication flow using the Figma MCP generate_diagram tool</code></li>
<li><code>generate a gantt chart for the project timeline using the Figma MCP generate_diagram tool</code></li>
<li><code>generate a sequence diagram for the payment processing system using the Figma MCP generate_diagram tool</code></li>
<li><code>generate an ERD for a blog database with users, posts, and comments using the Figma MCP generate_diagram tool</code></li>
<li><code>generate an architecture diagram for a real-time chat system using the Figma MCP generate_diagram tool</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Convert existing Mermaid syntax</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>create a diagram from this mermaid syntax: ...</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>

<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="get_code_connect_map">get_code_connect_map<a href="#get_code_connect_map" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to get_code_connect_map" title="Direct link to get_code_connect_map" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> Figma Design</p>
<p>Retrieves a mapping between selected Figma instance node IDs and their corresponding Code Connect components in your codebase.</p>
<p>It returns an object where each key is a Figma node ID (an instance in the current selection), and the value contains metadata about the connected component, such as:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>componentName</code>: The name of the component in your codebase.</li>
<li><code>source</code>: The location of the component in your codebase (file path or URL).</li>
<li><code>snippet</code>, <code>snippetImports</code>, <code>snippetNestedFunctions</code>: Snippet data when available.</li>
<li><code>version</code>: The source of the mapping (for example, Code Connect UI vs Code Connect CLI).</li>
<li><code>label</code>: The framework label (for example, <code>React</code>) when available.</li>
</ul>
<p>If multiple instances of the same component are selected, each instance appears as a separate entry. The mapping may also include nested components that have their own Code Connect mappings (for example, an icon inside a component).</p>
<p>On the remote server, you can use <code>clientFrameworks</code> and <code>clientLanguages</code> to control which Code Connect mappings are returned.</p>
<p>This mapping connects Figma design elements directly to their framework implementations, enabling design-to-code workflows and helping ensure the correct components are used for each part of the design.</p>

<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="get_metadata">get_metadata<a href="#get_metadata" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to get_metadata" title="Direct link to get_metadata" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> Figma Design</p>
<p>Returns a sparse XML representation of your selection containing just basic properties such as the layer IDs, names, types, position and sizes. This is an outline that your Agent can then break down and call <code>get_design_context</code> on to retrieve only the styling information of the design it needs. Useful for very large designs where <code>get_design_context</code> produces output with a large context size.</p>
<p>If you call <code>get_metadata</code> without a nodeId, the tool returns a list of the document's top-level pages (each entry shows the page's id and name) instead of an XML dump. Use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into, then call back with one of those page ids to fetch its structure. If you pass an invalid or unknown nodeId, the error response also includes that pages list so the agent has a usable recovery path. For richer per-page detail (child counts, top-level node types, etc.), <code>use_figma</code> can read the document structure directly via the Plugin API.</p>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="get_motion_context">get_motion_context<a href="#get_motion_context" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to get_motion_context" title="Direct link to get_motion_context" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> Figma Design</p>
<p>Returns keyframe animation data for an animated node so agents can faithfully recreate motion in code. The response includes an inventory of animated nodes, keyframe tracks with easing curves, pre-computed CSS <code>@keyframes</code> and <a href="https://motion.dev" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">motion.dev</a> code snippets, and timeline coordination hints that describe which nodes animate together.</p>
<p>Call <code>get_motion_context</code> after <code>get_design_context</code> when a design contains animation — <code>get_design_context</code> returns the static structure and styling, and <code>get_motion_context</code> supplies the motion layer. Pass the same node id you used for <code>get_design_context</code>. Set <code>recursive: true</code> to return motion data for every animated descendant of the selection in a single call.</p>

<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="weave_list_tools">weave_list_tools<a href="#weave_list_tools" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to weave_list_tools" title="Direct link to weave_list_tools" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> No file context required</p>
<p>Lists the authenticated user's Weave tools — published Weave workflows they can run — in their active Weave workspace.</p>
<p><strong>You can ask it to:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Browse your tools</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>show me my Weave tools</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Find a specific tool to run</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>list my Weave tools so I can pick one to run</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Parameters:</strong> None.</p>
<p><strong>Returns:</strong> For each tool, its name, creation date, and a link to open it in Weave.</p>
<hr>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="weave_get_tool_inputs">weave_get_tool_inputs<a href="#weave_get_tool_inputs" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to weave_get_tool_inputs" title="Direct link to weave_get_tool_inputs" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> No file context required</p>
<p>Gets the input contract of a Weave tool — the inputs you fill in to run it. Call before <code>weave_run_tool</code> to learn what to send.</p>
<p><strong>You can ask it to:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>See what a tool needs</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>what inputs does the "image generator" Weave tool take?</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Review current values before a run</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>show me the inputs and their defaults for this Weave tool</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Parameters:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>recipeId</code> — the id of the Weave tool (from <code>weave_list_tools</code>)</li>
<li><code>version</code> <em>(optional)</em> — tool version to inspect; omit for latest</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Returns:</strong> The resolved <code>version</code>, an <code>outputs</code> summary, and a flat <code>inputs</code> list (<code>nodeId</code>, <code>name</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>required</code>, <code>description</code>, <code>options</code>, <code>range</code>, <code>isIterator</code>, <code>default</code>).</p>
<hr>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="weave_upload_asset">weave_upload_asset<a href="#weave_upload_asset" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to weave_upload_asset" title="Direct link to weave_upload_asset" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> image (png, jpg/jpeg, webp, heic), video (mp4, mov, webm), audio (mp3, wav, ogg, and other common audio formats), and 3D model (glb, obj, fbx, ply)</p>
<p>Turns an attached file into a hosted URL to pass into <code>weave_run_tool</code>. Files already at a public https URL don't need this step.</p>
<p><strong>You can ask it to:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Use an attached image in a run</strong>
<ul>
<li>`use this image as the reference input for the Weave t</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Turn a local or attached file into a URL</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>upload this file to Weave so I can run a tool on it</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Parameters:</strong> <code>recipeId</code> — the Weave tool the asset is for.</p>
<p><strong>Returns:</strong> A single-use <code>submitUrl</code> to upload bytes to; after upload, the permanent hosted URL(s).</p>
<hr>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="weave_run_tool">weave_run_tool<a href="#weave_run_tool" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to weave_run_tool" title="Direct link to weave_run_tool" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> No file context required</p>
<p>Runs a Weave tool and returns run IDs to poll with <code>weave_get_tool_run_output</code>. Call <code>weave_get_tool_inputs</code> first.</p>
<p>Because running spends credits, this tool is gated: returns <code>inputs_required</code> if inputs are missing/invalid, or <code>cost_confirmation_required</code> with the credit cost — confirm with the user, then re-call with <code>acknowledgedCost</code> set.</p>
<p><strong>You can ask it to:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Run a tool with a prompt</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>run the "image generator" Weave tool with the prompt "a cat"</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Run a tool several times</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>run this Weave tool 3 times</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Parameters:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>recipeId</code></li>
<li><code>version</code> <em>(optional)</em></li>
<li><code>inputs</code> <em>(optional)</em> — an array of <code>{nodeId, value}</code></li>
<li><code>numberOfRuns</code> <em>(optional, 1–10)</em></li>
<li><code>acknowledgedCost</code> <em>(optional)</em></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Returns:</strong> <code>runIds</code> of started run(s), or a gate status.</p>
<hr>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="weave_get_tool_run_output">weave_get_tool_run_output<a href="#weave_get_tool_run_output" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to weave_get_tool_run_output" title="Direct link to weave_get_tool_run_output" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> No file context required</p>
<p>Gets the output and status of runs. Poll after running a tool.</p>
<p><strong>You can ask it to:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Check on a run</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>is my Weave run done yet?</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Get the latest output</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>show me the output of my last Weave run</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Parameters:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>recipeId</code></li>
<li><code>runIds</code> <em>(optional)</em></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Returns:</strong> Per-run status (RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELED), progress, error, and output(s) when complete.</p>
<hr>
<h3 class="anchor anchorWithStickyNavbar_IzjB" id="weave_cancel_tool_run">weave_cancel_tool_run<a href="#weave_cancel_tool_run" class="hash-link" aria-label="Direct link to weave_cancel_tool_run" title="Direct link to weave_cancel_tool_run" translate="no">​</a></h3>
<p><strong>Supported file types:</strong> No file context required</p>
<p>Cancels one or more in-progress runs. Cannot be undone.</p>
<p><strong>You can ask it to:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Stop a specific run</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>cancel that Weave run</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Stop everything running</strong>
<ul>
<li><code>cancel all my running Weave tool runs</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Parameters:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>recipeId</code></li>
<li><code>runIds</code> <em>(optional, omit to cancel all)</em></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Returns:</strong> Confirmation of canceled run(s).</p>
<hr>
